prompt: You remove every vertex in a maximum independent set from a simple graph. Why do the remaining vertices form a minimum vertex cover?

options.text: Independent sets and covers always have the same size
options.explanation: They partition the vertex set, and their sizes need not be equal.

options.text: Every edge has a remaining endpoint, and a smaller cover would leave a larger independent set
options.explanation: Both directions of the complement relationship establish optimality.

options.text: Each remaining vertex touches every edge
options.explanation: The set collectively touches every edge; no individual vertex has to do so.
This transformation complements the selected vertex set, not the graph’s edge set.

workedExample: An independent set contains no complete edge, so every edge has an endpoint among the remaining vertices. Those remaining vertices form a cover. In reverse, the complement of a cover contains no complete edge and is independent. Making one side largest makes the other smallest.

prompt: Which reduction shows that CLIQUE is NP-hard, given that Independent Set is?

options.explanation: A clique in G is generally not an independent set in G; the graph must be transformed.

options.text: Map (G, k) to (Ḡ, k), where Ḡ is the complement graph
options.explanation: Correct. A set with no edges in G has every edge in the complement graph, so independent sets of G are exactly cliques of the complement. Building the complement means checking every pair of vertices, about n²/2 pairs for n vertices.
That's the Independent Set to Vertex Cover reduction, not Clique.

options.text: Map a CLIQUE instance to an Independent Set instance
options.explanation: That direction shows CLIQUE is no harder than IS; to show CLIQUE is hard, reduce the known hard problem (IS) to CLIQUE.

workedExample: Start with the known hard Independent Set instance. Complement every edge between distinct vertices and keep the target size. A selected group has no internal edges before the transformation exactly when it has every internal edge afterwards. The polynomial construction therefore transfers Independent Set hardness to Clique.
